content.title: About
content.content: Summer squash soufflé is a light, airy dessert made from fresh summer squash, eggs, milk, and a touch of sugar. The squash gives a subtle sweet flavor and bright orange hue, while whipped egg whites create a fluffy texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Summer squash (Cucurbita pepo) is harvested early in the season when the flesh is tender and sweet.
Soufflé originated in France in the 17th century as a way to use egg whites for light dishes.
Squash is rich in beta‑carotene, which converts to vitamin A during cooking.
Traditionally, soufflés are baked at high heat to form a crisp top while staying soft inside.
In some regions, the dish is served with berry coulis or sprinkled with nuts for texture contrast.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene supports vision and immune function, converting to vitamin A after absorption.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Made mainly with egg whites and low‑fat milk, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Squash adds plant protein that complements the animal protein from eggs, improving the amino acid profile.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports normal blood pressure.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Squash fiber promotes healthy bowel function.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: The soufflé contains egg whites, which can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sugar is often added for sweetness; people monitoring blood glucose should watch portion size.

items.title: Undercooking risk
items.content: Insufficient baking may leave raw egg whites, increasing the risk of foodborne illness.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Squash can be mildly acidic; those with acid reflux should consume it in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the squash soufflé warm, dusted with powdered sugar, berry coulis, or toasted nuts. It works as a standalone dessert or paired with a dollop of light yogurt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the finished soufflé and store it in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2–3 days. Reheat gently in the oven or microwave to restore a light crust before serving.
